text: Did the authors use an analysis method that was appropriate to control for time-varying as well as baseline confounding?
Did the authors control for all the important baseline and time-varying confounding factors for which this was necessary?
Were confounding factors that were controlled for (and for which control was necessary) measured validly and reliably by the variables available in this study?
Did the authors control for time-varying factors or other variables measured after the start of intervention?
Did the use of negative controls, or other considerations, suggest serious uncontrolled confounding?
